title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}. The Deligne–Mumford compactification is stratified by Mumford–Deligne (stable) graphs G, with stratum M_G. A 'générisation' G → G' contracts a set C of edges of G, so that M_G lies in the closure of M_{G'}.

The torsor-like groupoid. M*_{G,G'} is the deleted tubular neighbourhood of M_G inside M_{G'}. It fibres over M_G with fibre a product of punctured discs, one for each edge in C. Its fundamental groupoid ΠM*_{G,G'} is therefore a canonical extension of ΠM_G by a Z^C-torsor (a local system of Z^C, twisted by graph automorphisms). This gives the specialization diagram (103) of the previous page:
  ΠM_G ←φ_{G,G'}— ΠM*_{G,G'} —r_{G,G'}→ ΠM_{G'}.

This page.
- The first lines finish describing the structure that ΠM*_{G,G'} inherits by passing to the generization G'. Grothendieck promises to return to 'the structure of this category, as a fibre product of categories, a bit further below'.
- He then names r_{G*,G'} the 'homomorphisme de générisation' on fundamental groupoids attached to G → G'.
- He announces a transitivity property for a composite generization (104) G → G' → G''. This composite gives rise to a diagram of groupoids, which is drawn but unfinished at the bottom of the page.

Next page. The diagram is completed as (105): ΠM*_{G,G''} is the 2-fibre product ΠM*_{G,G'} ×_{ΠM_{G'}} ΠM*_{G',G''}, so that r_{G,G''} factors through r_{G',G''}. Hence ΠM*_{G,G''} is an extension of ΠM_G by a Z^{C⊔C'}-torsor.

Geometric content. Near M_G the boundary is a normal crossings divisor (in the orbifold sense), with local model M_G × D^{C⊔C'}. The corner region (D*)^C × (D*)^{C'} is both the punctured neighbourhood of M_G in M_{G''} and the iterated neighbourhood. This justifies the 2-cartesian square.

Purpose. The aim is to assemble the fundamental groupoids of all strata, together with these specialization/generization correspondences, into a coherent system: a functor or 2-functor on the category of MD-graphs. This is the combinatorial-homotopical 'structure at infinity' underlying the Teichmüller tower and Lego of the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. Transitivity needs the local product (normal crossings) structure of the DM boundary and must be taken up to 2-isomorphism. It must also account for graph automorphisms, which is why one gets Z^C-torsors rather than trivial Z^C. Grothendieck handles this on the next page.
The machine transcription repeatedly reads 'torseur' where the image reads 'homom.' (homomorphisme).

ideas.what: Specialization/generization correspondence of fundamental groupoids for boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν}: ΠM_G ← ΠM*_{G,G'} → ΠM_{G'}, via deleted tubular neighbourhoods. ΠM*_{G,G'} is an extension of ΠM_G by a Z^C-torsor.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / homotopy links of strata; Dehn-twist extensions of boundary stabilizers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara–Nakamura (1990s), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Boggi; in topology Quinn (homotopy links)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and structure at infinity, but not this formalism explicitly.

ideas.what: Transitivity: for G → G' → G'', ΠM*_{G,G''} ≃ ΠM*_{G,G'} ×^{2}_{ΠM_{G'}} ΠM*_{G',G''}, with composite generization homomorphism.
ideas.modern_name: Composition of homotopy links / exit-path (∞-)category of a stratified space; modular-operad-type coherence of boundary inclusions
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson, Treumann (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; for M̄_{g,n}, the modular operad/GT literature (Horel, Boavida–Horel–Robertson)

ideas.what: Description of the category of strata/generizations as a fibre product of categories (announced).
ideas.modern_name: Category of stable graphs with contractions (Getzler–Kapranov graph category)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, for the DM stratification of M̄_{g,ν}, essentially the exit-path / homotopy-link data of a stratified space. This means fundamental groupoids of strata, groupoids of punctured tubular neighbourhoods, and 2-cartesian composition along chains of strata. He presents it as a 2-categorical gluing datum for the 'structure at infinity', predating the stratified-homotopy (exit path ∞-category) formalism and its use for moduli of curves.
missed.quote: L'homom r_{G*,G'} s'appellera l'homom de générisation sur les groupoïdes fondamentaux ... On va dégager une propriété de transitivité pour ces homom. de générisation
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links GT/Teichmüller-Lego theory to exit-path categories of the DM stratification. That framework is now used in profinite/operadic approaches to GT, but its explicit origin with Grothendieck is not recorded.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, natural formalization (punctured neighbourhoods, Z^C extensions, 2-cartesian transitivity) consistent with the Esquisse program. Each piece is known to specialists in later language, but the explicit stratified-groupoid gluing formalism in Grothendieck's hand is unpublished detail.
